title: A nontrivial finite purely inseparable extension has a degree-p intermediate step
statement: Let $L/K$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] of characteristic $p>0$ with $[L:K]>1$. Then there are an intermediate field $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$ and an element $z\in L$ such that $[M:K]<[L:K]$, $L=M(z)$, $z^p=f$ for some $f\in M$, and $[L:M]=p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring), proof, induction paragraph: choose $K\subset M\subset L$ with $L/M$ a degree-$p$ extension obtained by adjoining a $p$th root
